name: Tuomo Suntola
summary: Finnish physicist, inventor of atomic layer epitaxy (ALE/ALD) and of the Humicap humidity sensor, later Chief Scientist at Lohja and founder of Microchemistry Ltd.

name: Riikka L. Puurunen
summary: ALD researcher at VTT Technical Research Centre of Finland, author of the essay.

name: Thor Stubb
summary: Professor heading the Electron Physics laboratory at Helsinki University of Technology, Suntola's doctoral-era supervisor.

name: Tapio Wiik
summary: Colleague of Suntola at the VTT Semiconductor Laboratory who pre-studied humidity sensing.

name: Jorma Antson
summary: Co-developer of the Humicap humidity sensor and co-inventor on the 1974 ALE patent.

name: Sven Lindfors
summary: Suntola's closest co-worker in ALE reactor design, co-inventor on the 1979 ALE patent, co-founder of Picosun Oy.

name: Arto Pakkala
summary: Member of Suntola's ALE-EL team, co-inventor on the 1979 ALE patent.

name: Ralf Graeffe
summary: Member of the Lohja ALE-EL team who inspected the airport test display modules.

name: Antti Piippo
summary: Business-oriented manager of Lohja's Display Electronics division, later owner of Elcoteq.

name: Ahti Aintila
summary: Led driving-circuitry and manufacturing technology development for EL panels at Lohja, founder of Picopack Oy.

name: Tapio Alvesalo
summary: Head of Neste's NAPS venture team who proposed applying ALE to thin film solar panels.

name: Jaakko Hyvärinen
summary: Microchemistry PV researcher who built the Quicksun flash solar simulator and founded Endeas Oy.

name: Aimo Rautiainen
summary: One of the first chemists in the Microchemistry team.

name: Eeva-Liisa Lakomaa
summary: One of the first chemists in the Microchemistry team.

name: Marina Lindblad
summary: Microchemistry researcher whose doctoral thesis covered quantum chemical analysis of ZnS ALE growth.

name: Suvi Haukka
summary: Microchemistry catalyst researcher who completed a doctoral dissertation on ALE.

name: Arla Kytökivi
summary: Microchemistry catalyst researcher who completed a doctoral dissertation on ALE.

name: Matti Ervasti
summary: Business-oriented managing director who succeeded Suntola at Microchemistry.

name: Kustaa Poutiainen
summary: Co-founder of Picosun Oy with Sven Lindfors.

name: Pekka Soininen
summary: Started the ALE reactor activity at Beneq Oy.

name: Jun-ichi Nishizawa
summary: Japanese professor (Semiconductor Laboratory, Sendai) who pursued ALE growth of GaAs under the name Molecular Layer Epitaxy.

name: Salah Bedair
summary: North Carolina State University professor who demonstrated ALE of GaAs in a CVD system.

name: DenBaars
summary: University of Southern California professor whose group demonstrated ALD of GaAs in atmospheric MOCVD.

name: Lauri Niinistö
summary: Professor of inorganic and analytical chemistry at HUT, long-term ALE collaborator of Suntola and chair of ALE-1.

name: Markku Leskelä
summary: University of Helsinki professor co-heading the Finnish Centre of Excellence in Atomic Layer Deposition.

name: Mikko Ritala
summary: University of Helsinki professor co-heading the Finnish Centre of Excellence in Atomic Layer Deposition.

name: Tapani Pakkanen
summary: University of Joensuu professor who collaborated on quantum chemical analysis of ZnS ALE growth.

name: M. Ahonen
summary: Graduate student at Tampere University of Technology who took up ALE of group III-V semiconductors.

name: Markus Pessa
summary: Professor of physics at Tampere University of Technology who directed group III-V MBE research.

name: Victor Drozd
summary: Leningrad researcher on molecular layering who invited Suntola to meet Aleskovskii.

name: V. B. Aleskovskii
summary: Soviet professor at the University of Leningrad, co-originator of molecular layering.

name: S. I. Kol'tsov
summary: Soviet professor, co-originator of molecular layering with Aleskovskii.

name: Ulf Ström
summary: Managing director of Finlux Inc., responsible for marketing ALE-EL panels in the USA.

name: Heli Vaara
summary: Assistant to Tuomo Suntola at Microchemistry.

name: Stanley Myers
summary: President & CEO of SEMI (USA) who presented the European SEMI Award to Suntola.

name: Olarinluoma
summary: District of Espoo where Lohja's large EL production facility was built.

name: Lohja
summary: Finnish town where the Kunnarla pilot production plant for TF-EL displays was located.

name: Helsinki University of Technology
summary: Finnish technical university where Suntola studied electrical engineering and earned his doctorate.

name: VTT Semiconductor Laboratory
aliases: Semiconductor Laboratory of VTT Technical Research Centre of Finland
summary: Laboratory established as part of Thor Stubb's Electron Physics laboratory at HUT, later part of VTT.

name: VTT Technical Research Centre of Finland
summary: Finnish national technical research centre.

name: Vaisala Oy
summary: Finnish company specializing in meteorological instrumentation, user of the Humicap sensor.

name: INSKO
summary: Finnish engineering organizations' training centre where Suntola lectured.

name: Instrumentarium Oy
summary: Finnish trading house importing medical instrumentation, where the ALE-EL project began.

name: Datex Oy
summary: Small technology company established by Instrumentarium.

name: Lohja Oy
summary: Finnish building material company that bought the ALE-EL project and became the world's third EL manufacturer.

name: Aspo Oy
summary: Finnish company from which Antti Piippo was recruited to Lohja.

name: Finlux Inc.
summary: US marketing company for Lohja's ALE-EL panels.

name: Planar Inc.
summary: American EL display manufacturer that acquired Lohja's EL business.

name: Planar International
summary: Finnish EL activity operating as a subsidiary of Planar Inc.

name: Beneq Oy
summary: Finnish company operating the Olarinluoma EL plant and manufacturing ALE reactors.

name: Picopack Oy
summary: Company founded by Ahti Aintila to produce smart cards using TAB technology.

name: Elcoteq Oy
summary: Contract electronics manufacturer separated from Lohja's microelectronics division.

name: Neste Oy
summary: Finnish national oil company, parent of Microchemistry Ltd.

name: Neste Advanced Power Systems
summary: Neste's corporate venture unit for renewable energy solutions.

name: Microchemistry Ltd.
summary: Neste subsidiary set up by Suntola for ALE-based solar panels and catalysis, later focused on ALE reactors.

name: ASM
summary: Dutch semiconductor equipment company that acquired Microchemistry.

name: ASM Microchemistry
summary: Finnish ALE activity of ASM continuing from Microchemistry Ltd.

name: Picosun Oy
summary: Finnish ALD reactor company founded by Sven Lindfors and Kustaa Poutiainen.

name: Endeas Oy
summary: Company producing Quicksun solar simulators, founded by Jaakko Hyvärinen.

name: University of Helsinki
summary: University hosting the Laboratory of Inorganic Chemistry and the Finnish ALD Centre of Excellence.

name: Finnish Centre of Excellence in Atomic Layer Deposition
summary: Academy of Finland Centre of Excellence in ALD headed by Leskelä and Ritala.

name: Tampere University of Technology
summary: Finnish technical university where Suntola lectured as docent.

name: University of Joensuu
summary: Finnish university where Tapani Pakkanen worked on quantum chemistry of ALE.

name: University of Leningrad
summary: Soviet university where Aleskovskii's molecular layering group worked.

name: North Carolina State University
summary: US university where Bedair's group demonstrated ALE of GaAs.

name: University of Southern California
summary: US university where DenBaars's group demonstrated ALD of GaAs.

name: CGE
summary: Big French state-owned company that sought an ALE-EL license from Lohja.

name: Sintra Alcatel
summary: French state-owned company to which the ALE-EL license was granted.

name: Society for Information Display
summary: Professional society whose conferences hosted the first ALE-EL disclosure.

name: Materials Research Society
summary: Society whose 1994 Annual Meeting hosted Suntola's ALE talk.

name: Fortum Oyj
summary: Finnish energy company formed from the fusion of Neste and IVO.

name: Fortum Foundation
summary: Foundation for which Suntola served as attorney.

name: World Energy Council
summary: International energy organization of which Suntola was a member.

name: SEMI
summary: Semiconductor industry association that awards the European SEMI Award.

name: Physics Foundations Society
summary: Society chaired by Suntola, publisher of his books.

name: Finnish Society for Natural Philosophy
summary: Society in which Suntola is a board member and lecturer.

name: Goskhimizdat
summary: Leningrad publisher of the 1965 molecular layering conference abstract.

name: Humicap humidity sensor
summary: Thin polymer film capacitive humidity sensor developed by Suntola and Antson for Vaisala.

name: Humidity sensor patent US 4 164 868
summary: Suntola's international patent underlying the Humicap sensor.

name: Atomic Layer Epitaxy
summary: Thin film growth technique based on repeated separate, saturating gas-solid reactions.

summary: First international ALE patent by Suntola and Antson covering the basic ALE concept.

name: ALE patent FIN 57975 / US 4 413 022
summary: Second international ALE patent covering the inert gas reactor and EL processes.

name: LCD color display patent US 4 907 862
summary: Suntola's patent on electronically controllable color elements and sequential color display.

name: F-120 reactor
summary: Compact research ALE reactor from Microchemistry, the first commercial ALD reactor.

name: F-450 reactor
summary: Microchemistry ALE reactor for silicon wafers and 450 mm x 450 mm glass substrates.

name: 1980 SID Outstanding Paper Award
summary: SID award for the ALE-EL paper by Suntola, Antson, Pakkala and Lindfors.

name: European SEMI Award 2004
summary: Award honoring the pioneer in atomic layer deposition techniques.

name: Suntola 1989 review paper (Mater. Sci. Reports)
summary: Suntola's review of ALE mapping known laboratories working on ALE.

name: The Dynamic Universe – toward a unified picture of physical reality
summary: Suntola's book presenting a holistic picture of physical reality.

name: The Short History of Science – or the long path to the union of metaphysics and empiricism
summary: Suntola's book linking philosophical considerations to historical development of science.

name: Some characteristics of molecular layering reactions
summary: 1965 conference abstract by Aleskovskii and Kol'tsov on molecular layering.

name: First Symposium on Atomic Layer Epitaxy
summary: First specific ALE conference, organized by VTT Semiconductor Laboratory in Espoo.
